unit: EUR bn, current prices; USD->EUR at ECB annual averages (2022 1.0530, 2023 1.0813, 2024 1.0824, 2025 1.1300, 2026 Jan-Aug 1.1629); low/high = ~90% range
method: reexports_to_RUS: the part of each hub's RECORDED exports to Russia (inside trade_full exports_to_RUS) that is made elsewhere. Where the hub flags re-exports (UAE, Georgia), the flag is used. Elsewhere, for each HS2 manufactured chapter (28-40, 42-43, 61-70, 73, 82-96): matched increase = min(increase in exports to Russia over the 2019-21 average, increase in imports from non-Russian partners over 2019-21), times a hub-specific share that is a genuine re-export (see reasoning). Low uses 0.75x the import increase as the cap; high uses 1.5x (no cap for hubs that under-record imports: KAZ, KGZ, MNG, TJK). A baseline level of re-exports (2019-21) is added: matched baseline flow in net-import chapters x a hub share. origin_shares: increase of the hub's HS84/85/87/90 imports by origin country (customs origin) over 2021 (KAZ: 2019), mixed with the 2021 import structure for the baseline part, weighted over years; low/high = yearly min x0.75 / max x1.25. Applied to all chapters. reexports_from_RUS: Russian goods passed on = min(increase of hub imports from Russia in HS71 (gold, diamonds) or HS27 (fuel), increase of hub exports of the same chapter to non-Russian partners) x pass-through share. destination_shares = increase of those exports by partner (first onward hop only). 2026_JanAug = 2025 share x trade_full Jan-Aug 2026 (not annualized), range widened by 0.8/1.2. Missing Comtrade years use the latest model share x trade_full totals.
how_to_apply: In the map, for each hub and year: move reexports_to_RUS x (1 - hub_margin_share) from the hub to the origin countries according to origin_shares (the hub keeps the margin); move reexports_from_RUS x (1 - from_RUS margin) from the hub's imports from Russia to destination_shares. To get the change against the pre-war level, subtract reexports_to_RUS_baseline_2019_2021 in the same way. "other" in origin_shares includes VNM (Samsung phones made in Vietnam), GBR, CZE, POL, ESP, IND, MEX (see origin_other_detail).

hub_margin_share.reasoning: Margin = (re-export sales value - cost of the goods bought abroad) / sales value. Educated guess, no direct source: wholesale gross margins are typically 5-20% of sales; pure pass-through traders in a re-export hub work at the low end, intermediaries taking sanctions or compliance risk on Russia-bound goods at the high end. residual.json used the same 5-20% band. For onward Russian gold and diamonds the margin is far smaller (bullion dealing and refining margins are around 0.5-3% of value; Armenian cutting and jewellery work adds a little more); for fuel, 3-12% (trading and logistics).

overlap_with_residual: No double counting. residual.json adds to origin countries the goods that are MISSING from partner-reported exports to Russia: the rise in the mirror gap between partners' reported exports to KGZ/KAZ and those hubs' own recorded imports (transit_KGZ EUR 3.2/5.8/6.7/8.6bn, transit_KAZ EUR 0.6/1.1/4.2/2.9bn, 2022-2025), which by construction never appear in KGZ/KAZ exports to Russia either. The figures here move value that IS recorded in the hubs' own exports to Russia (part of trade_full exports_to_RUS) from the hub to origin countries; the matched-import cap uses the hubs' RECORDED imports, so the same goods cannot be in the mirror gap. Two caveats: (1) for the high bounds of KAZ/KGZ the import cap is dropped, so some high-bound value could in principle also be in the mirror gap; treat the KAZ/KGZ highs as not additive with residual highs. (2) residual's pro-rata "residual" component (EUR 11-21bn) is distributed over all countries by their reported exports to Russia, including hubs; if the map moves hub re-exports to origins, the hub's pro-rata share should be moved in the same proportion (reexport_share_of_exports_to_RUS). Georgia's car re-exports to KGZ/KAZ/ARM are not counted here at all (they show up in those hubs or in residual transit). Hong Kong's onward gold to mainland China is handled in residual.json and not repeated here.
notes: Total re-exports to Russia across the 11 hubs (central): EUR 7.4bn (2022), 11.3bn (2023), 9.0bn (2024), 8.7bn (2025). UAE, KAZ, ARM and TUR are ~90%. The rise in re-exports covers ~90-100% of the extra exports to Russia for ARE, 50-70% for ARM/KAZ/KGZ, 25-35% for TUR/AZE and 5-15% for UZB. Most transit to Russia via KGZ/KAZ is unrecorded and lives in residual.json.

China via third countries: weighted over hubs (2023), origin shares are CHN ~35%, named coalition origins (DEU, USA, JPN, KOR, ITA, FRA) 28% plus other EU/GBR in "other" (~8-12%), VNM 7%. China is the largest origin for KGZ, UZB, MNG, KAZ, AZE and ARE; combined with residual.json (China 61-65% of KGZ transit), China is the main origin of hub-routed goods.

Origin shares are by customs country of origin, so brand owners differ: Samsung phones count as Vietnam, Apple as China. Imports recorded from the UAE or other hubs (e.g. ARE in GEO or KGZ data) stay in "other".

HS2 aggregation hides domestic production within chapters; that is what the hub-specific shares and wide ranges try to cover. Hub-specific shares are educated guesses calibrated on: Armenian finance ministry (87% of export growth to Russia were re-exports, H1 2023), S&P Global (30-50% foreign origin in Turkey's high-priority shipments), and the UAE/Georgia re-export flags.

Onward Russian gold/diamonds: ARM peak 2024 (EUR ~6bn) collapsed in 2025 as re-exports to the UAE fell; UAE onward gold proxied. Destinations are first hop only (Armenian gold goes to the UAE and is then traded on to CHE, IND, HKG, TUR).
Turkey's refined-product exports from Russian crude (processed_from_RUS_not_counted) are not re-exports under rules of origin; include them only if the map wants a "refining loophole" view.

Certainty: B = hub publishes a re-export flag (UAE, Georgia); C = matched-trade estimate with an official calibration point (ARM, KAZ, KGZ); D = matched-trade estimate with assumed shares (TUR, UZB, AZE, MNG, TJK, SRB).
